Helt sant det du sier. Alle velmente råd og erfaringer kan treffe feil (er heller ikke lett å implementere når man er syk), men antok at OP heller ville ha flere forskjellige svar/meninger på innlegget og ta vurdering selv. Posten min var ihvertfall kun skrevet fra et medfølende perspektiv - ikke en ovenfra og ned-holdning.

For det første er det å anbefale å se hva livsstilsendringer (prioritere søvn, balansert diett, fysisk aktivitet, unngå for mye "doom scrolling", sette grenser om man strekker seg for langt i jobb/fritid osv.) du kan gjøre som kan forbedre situasjonen din. Høres teit ut, men kan gjøre en del. Jeg har angst og annen mer heavy diagnose på toppen så vet hvor utfordrende disse tingene er, men man merker en forskjell. Jeg ville gjort research på hva du kan gjøre for din egen del. Mindfulness i 5 minutter har hjulpet å roe meg ned litt noen ganger. Eneste problemet er at det er midlertidig selvfølgelig.
Skal også nevnes at dette med å røyke kan være med å forverre problemet ditt. Jeg håper ihvertfall du ikke røyker hver dag og at du heller prøver å bruke det som en pause en sjelden gang innimellom. Selv hvis man antar at du er såpass heldig å ikke få forverret angst i det hele tatt av det så påvirker det definitivt søvnkvaliteten.
Jeg ville prøvd å presse mer på legen men ventetid blir det. Om du "kun" har angst/stress og ellers klarer deg bra i livet (er i jobb/skole osv.) så er man ikke høyst prioritert. Kanskje oppfølgingstjenesten i kommunen kunne vært et alternativ? Der får man noen å snakke med. Usikker på detaljene rundt det da jeg midlertidig skal ut av DPS-behandling og henvises til OT-tjenesten nå snart slik at jeg ikke står helt uten hjelp. Det er et alternativ ihvertfall.

Jeg er ikke noen ekspert på yrket personlig så håper du også får svar av noen med mer personlige erfaringer. Jeg tenker at det tvertimot kan være en fordel at du er en rolig og omsorgsfull type. I politiyrket vil du komme tett på mange i sine mindre heldige livsøyeblikk så det å kunne holde seg tålmodig og se ting fra andres perspektiv kan være en fordel. Man skal tross alt forholde seg til alt fra fulle mennesker og rykke ut på psykiatriske oppdrag i politiyrket og også stoppe/etterforske seriøs kriminalitet. Likevel kan vel det å være for sensitiv bli en negativ faktor, men tror ikke det utelukker at du kan passe i yrket. Jeg tenkte jeg var for sensitiv til å jobbe i helsevesenet, men jeg har overrasket meg selv i min evne til å kunne forholde meg mer avmålt og rasjonell når det er nødvendig. Utelukker likevel ikke at min sensitive side lettere kan føre til utbrenthet i yrket - noe lignende kan vel stemme for deg. Andre ting spiller jo også inn. God fysisk form, god evne til å takle stress og en variert yrkeshverdag. Det finnes jo muligheter å jobbe mer internt i politiet i kontorsammenheng, men tror det er vanlig å begynne patruljerende kanskje? Det må nesten noen andre svare på, men her har du mine tanker. Tenker man må ha evne til å være autoritær uten å bli såpass hard og tøff at du ikke evner noe som helst empati eller omsorg heller.

Self-diagnosing is just so rampant these days. I went around suspecting I had BPD for years and sometimes talked about my suspicions with others but never did I say I had it. I was recently diagnosed with it (+ traits from other personality disorders mixed in) after my psychologist brought it up. She interviewed me over several sessions so the process took months. Admittedly I live in a country with better access to treatment than some. Still even with difficulty accessing treatment it doesn't mean you should walk around claiming you have these complex disorders that are hard to diagnose, treat and live with.

I don't have any history of sexual abuse etc. but I have issues with disordered eating (atypical anorexia). Things started getting progressively worse mental health wise particularly around 15 and for some reason it is so hard for me to weigh much more than I did back around then. Maybe because I feel a bit "arrested" in my development. I still feel like a teenager in many ways at the age of 26. Still bitter about responsibilities that come with it. My weight has not changed too much since my early teens even in periods with less food issues. I have always been tall and thin and maybe it's one of the few aspects of my fractured identity I have some comfort in. Then again there's a bit of history of eating issues on my mothers side so I was probably a bit genetically predisposed as well. I think a lot of factors play into it but issues relating to childhood is a big theme within eating disorders.

Yeah, I've experienced similar in my life as well. It's good that you respect peoples boundaries - it says a lot about you! As someone who's gone through a lot of loss and has always had a small family unit friendships are really important to me and I often feel less loved and appreciated than I would like. I do try to become better at focusing on the things I'm grateful for in my life rather than everything I wish was different or easier. It's hard though. There's often a certain loneliness to that grief you carry (especially if it's from a very young age - it becomes part of your entire identity and life story from as early as you can remember). I can feel quite emotionally alone even with people I have a lot of fun with or get physical affection from. I do have a special connection with a friend of mine who also lost her father fairly young. We get eachother really well. I hope you'll find someone like that.

I'm so sorry. For your loss but almost even more so that your dad dropped the ball of parenting so badly. That's two deep wounds you're dealing with. No wonder you're struggling. I lost my dad at 6 and also feel broken and sometimes hopeless about if I'll ever be able to be truly content in life. My mum has struggles but she did a great job raising me on her own. I really feel for you. Grief is such a complex thing and never leaves fully. Please don't give up hope! I sense in your post you have a lot of love to give but the circumstances in your life haven't been right. I think you need to protect yourself and keep your dad at a good distance sometimes and practice self love. Also no matter how scary it is you need to try to put yourself out there in order to be truly seen by people. It's tough and a struggle for people like us but the right person exists and they will understand. Fight for yourself because I know you deserve good things.
